newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia gold output seen down, integration urged.
newsitem.headline: Russia gold output seen down, integration urged.

text.p: Russia's gold output may fall to 90 tonnes in 1997 from 110-117 tonnes this year unless hundreds of Russia's gold mining firms integrate into big groups, a government official said on Wednesday.

Itar-Tass news agency quoted Vladimir Piskunov, the head of the industry ministry's precious metals and stones department, as telling a meeting of producers that the gold sector had reached a crisis this year.
Output fell more than 10 percent on 1995 levels, Piskunov said. Government officials have said last year's gold output was between 122 and 135 tonnes.
Some data include gold production from scrap.
Piskunov said the only way out of the crisis was to create financial-industrial groups (FIGs), or state-backed conglomerates around big banks, linking all stages of gold production.
He said there were too many gold mining firms with different kinds of ownership, about 700, which created chaos in the formerly fully state-controlled industry.

Many FIGs are active in Russia in sectors including chemicals, telecommunications, metals, shipbuilding and car construction. The FIGs also reflect a wider urge to re-establish ties broken after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
Piskunov said ownership rights on the produced gold and a reduction in taxes, which currently take away about 60 percent of the gold mined by companies, would help the industry recover.

Earlier this year Russian producers predicted a fall in 1996 output to 100-105 tonnes, and pinned the blame for the poor state of the industry on the absence of a viable precious metals market and a metals exchange.
An industry ministry report also noted that growing criminality in the gold sector has dealt a heavy blow to production, Tass said on Tuesday.
Producers have said that about five percent of all mined gold leaks to the black market, where some producers prefer to get cash at once instead of waiting for months for the government to pay.
Piskunov said the government owed gold producers about 1.6 trillion roubles.
